claim.summary: For a monic polynomial F without real zeros, with u zeros above the real line and l below (n = u + l), F#(z) = conj F(conj z) and A_theta = F + e^{i theta} F#: if e^{i theta} != -1 then A_theta has degree n, at least |u - l| distinct real zeros and at most 2 min(u, l) nonreal zeros; if e^{i theta} = -1 it vanishes identically exactly when F has real coefficients, and otherwise has degree below n and at least |u - l| - 1 distinct real zeros.
claim.assessment: Working proof: on the real line A_theta = 2 e^{i theta/2} |F| cos(arg F - theta/2), the argument of F changes by pi (u - l) along the line, and the intermediate value theorem gives the real zeros; the degree bounds the rest.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

claim.summary: For T > 0 and 0 < eps <= T^2/4, F(z) = (z - i)(z - T + i eps) has one zero above the real line and one below, while F + F# = 2 (z^2 - T z + eps) has only real zeros (a double one at eps = T^2/4; at T = 20, eps = 100 the lower zero is 20 - 100i): one sum function with all zeros on the line does not place the configuration on one side, at any distance of the minority zero.
claim.assessment: Working proof by expansion of the product and the discriminant T^2 - 4 eps.

claim.summary: For a monic polynomial F of degree n without real zeros, A_theta = F + e^{i theta} F# and N(theta) the number of distinct real zeros of A_theta: (1/(2 pi)) int_{-pi}^{pi} N d theta = (1/pi) int_R |(arg F)'| dx = n - (2/pi) int min(P, Q) dx, P and Q the sums of |Im z_j|/|x - z_j|^2 over the zeros above and below the line; the mean is n exactly when all zeros are on one side, and if A_theta is real-rooted for almost every theta then all zeros of F are on one side.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the real zeros of A_theta are level sets of arg F, and the integral of the number of preimages equals the total variation; a multiple real zero occurs for finitely many theta.

significance.rationale: Decides the converse left open by one sum function: the whole family determines one-sidedness, and the mean number of nonreal zeros is an explicit integral.

claim.summary: For a nonempty finite multiset R with Phi(s) = sum m_rho/(s - rho): all Re rho <= sigma_0 iff Re Phi > 0 on Re s > sigma_0. For real points Gamma and one conjugate pair gamma +- i delta of multiplicity m, the Laguerre expression L(x) = sum m_w/(x - w)^2 on the real line is negative at x = gamma iff sum over Gamma of m'/(gamma - gamma')^2 < 2m/delta^2, the pair's term is at least -2m/delta^2 and negative only for |x - gamma| < delta, and L >= 0 everywhere when the real points have gaps at most 2 delta/sqrt(m) covering (gamma - delta, gamma + delta).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proofs. The half-plane sign criterion is equivalent to the zero-free statement at every boundary, so it is not a weaker premise; the local real-line (Laguerre, phase-monotonicity) condition cannot fail for an off-line pair farther from the line than half the gap of the real points around it times sqrt(m), while the global count of real zeros detects every pair and is the goal's statement. Finite configurations only; part (a) is the finite model of a known equivalence and no novelty is claimed; the general Hermite-Biehler and de Branges sources are not read.
